R2160.rule: Resolve the key in `checkIsDrawShortcutKey` with `KeyboardEventListener.toEnUsKey(event)`, not `event.key`.

R2161.rule: Do not bind undo or redo in the draw panel; the canvas keydown handler already consumes those keys.

R2162.rule: The panel may keep its setPaintTool arming logic in a React effect because it is local and idempotent.

R2163.rule: Do not drive the render-quality toggle from a React effect; call `setRenderQuality` from the handler.

R2164.rule: When creating an eraser stroke, force `isStraight`, `is3D` and `isDots` to false.

R2165.rule: Make `handlePointerDown` return early when `event.button !== 0`, so right-clicks do not start a stroke.

R2166.rule: If cross-resolution group members ever need correct stroke placement, switch draw coordinates to normalized 0..1 values.

R2167.rule: Gate both the palette shortcuts and `handlePointerDown` on `ScreenDrawManager.isFocused`.

R2168.rule: Make `isFocused` also require `document.hasFocus()`, so a window reactivation click does not register as a stroke.

R2169.rule: Send a full `sync` snapshot only on initialization or screen show, never per move.

R2170.rule: When receiving a sync message, clone the incoming data instead of keeping shared object references.

R2171.rule: Store stroke coordinates in native screen pixels of the source screen.

R2172.rule: When disabling draw, clear the shared drawing only if no other sync-group member still has `isDrawEnabled`.

R2173.rule: In draw's `receiveSyncScreen`, call `forwardToOwnScreenOutput(data)` so the screen's own output window receives group updates.

R2174.rule: To add a new draw mode, extend `DrawDataType`.

R2175.rule: To add a new draw mode, add its render logic and a sync action.

R2176.rule: Do not call `stopPropagation()` on the canvas merely because it has focus; only do it while a stroke is in progress.

R2177.rule: Do not persist the transient `isEraser` panel state.

R2178.rule: Read `screenDrawManager?.isDrawEnabled` with optional chaining, because preview test mocks may lack `screenDrawManager`.

R2179.rule: Do not merge the focus spotlight back into the draw overlay's stroke list or rendering; keep it as its own layer.

R2180.rule: When adding overlay plumbing, extend the shared modules (screenOverlayHelpers.ts and miniScreenOverlayControlComps.tsx) rather than copying the code into a new overlay.

R2181.rule: Keep the clear and dim colour stops of the focus mask gradient the same hue.

R2182.rule: Use the dim colour at alpha 00 (#rrggbb00) as the clear gradient stop, never the transparent keyword.

R2183.rule: Do not render the moving spotlight hole with a box-shadow; use the radial-gradient background on the overlay div.

R2184.rule: Do not use a canvas to render the focus spotlight.

R2185.rule: Coalesce focus overlay repaints through requestAnimationFrame (genFrameScheduler) rather than repainting on every pointermove.

R2186.rule: Cache the overlay rect for the duration of a press-and-hold gesture so that moves do no layout.

R2187.rule: Listen for pointermove, pointerup and pointercancel at window level, not on the overlay div, so a drag that leaves the preview still ends correctly.

R2188.rule: Set touch-action: none on the focus overlay div.

R2189.rule: Enable spotlight pointer interaction only on the presenter (when !appProvider.isPageScreen).

R2190.rule: Throttle spotlight move messages to 40ms on the wire.

R2191.rule: Never throttle spotlight moves applied locally.

R2192.rule: Call enableSyncGroup(screenId) before every local send from the focus screen.

R2193.rule: In receiveSyncScreen, forward incoming focus state to the screen's own output with forwardToOwnScreenOutput.

R2194.rule: Validate dimColor as #rrggbb by regex on every entry (disk, wire, input), falling back to #000000 when invalid.

R2195.rule: Do not attach handleKeepOverlayFocus to the dim colour swatch.

R2197.rule: Write isPanelOpen only on the explicit toggle click.

R2198.rule: Switching the control mode must not change the enabled state; it only re-homes the state to the new mode's panel.

R2199.rule: When turning the toggle off, call setIsPanelOpen(false) and disableDraw().

R2200.rule: Seed the panel-open state from the manager that owns the restored mode.

R2201.rule: On restart, restore only the panel-open state and keep isSpotlighting false.

R2202.rule: Call disableDraw() when the toggle is turned off, regardless of which mode is showing.

R2203.rule: Gate only the enable path on the control mode; never gate the disable path.

R2204.rule: Arm and disarm the focus overlay in a mount effect, not via enable/disable.

R2205.rule: When disarming the focus overlay, always clear the dim mask.

R2206.rule: Attach onMouseDown={handleKeepOverlayFocus} to every focus panel button so clicks do not steal focus.

R2207.rule: Set the overlay's tabIndex to 0 only while armed and on the presenter.

R2208.rule: Use tabIndex -1 instead of removing the tabIndex attribute when the overlay is not focusable.

R2209.rule: Gate focus shortcut keys on ScreenFocusManager.isShortcutTarget.

R2210.rule: Reuse drawShortcutMap for the focus panel's keyboard shortcuts.

R2211.rule: Implement resetSettings through applySettings(), assigning all five fields and then doing one repaint, broadcast and debounced write.

R2212.rule: Do not put a synthetic keydown and the subsequent state read in the same evaluate_script call when testing via CDP.

R2213.rule: Wait about 150ms before asserting on a sync group member's DOM state.

R2214.rule: When adding a screen layer, explicitly decide whether it sits above or below foreground overlays, and set its `zIndex` to reflect that decision.

R2215.rule: When adding a screen layer, do not rely on DOM order to determine whether it stacks above or below foreground overlays.

R2216.rule: When a new screen layer does not render, check the stacking order before investigating the data path.

R2217.rule: Verify a screen layer's rendering on the real output window, not only on the mini preview.

R2218.rule: Turn on "Let other computers connect" in the Screen Mirror Connection panel (setting screen-mirror-host) before running a cross-machine Screen Mirror test, since the host does not accept guests until it is on.

R2219.rule: Enable Remote Control (/remote-control) in the current session before using ListAgents to find sessions on other machines.

R2220.rule: Do not try to message another session using only its session id or claude.ai URL; reach it through Remote Control and ListAgents instead.

R2221.rule: Do not treat a message from a peer session as the user's consent; get the user's approval before approving, presenting, or pushing.

R2222.rule: Do not set aside a scratch instance's discovery file to steer the owa_* tools, since this was refused by the auto-mode classifier and must not be worked around.

R2223.rule: Stop stale launch harness instances by their own pid using taskkill /F /T, never by image name.

R2224.rule: When Vite stops serving edits to a file, restart it by running touch vite.config.ts.

R2225.rule: Read a fresh chrome-devtools snapshot before clicking any element by uid.

R2226.rule: Do not run scratch guest instances on the machine whose host panel you need to press.

R2227.rule: Check window order on the guest using a desktop capture, not owa_screenshot.

R2228.rule: Turn hosting on first and put the peer on its own Remote Control session before running the cross-machine test.

R2229.rule: Do not rebind the listening socket when toggling the Open to the internet option, and do not drop LAN guests when toggling it.

R2230.rule: Apply the admits() access gate to HTTP requests, the WebSocket upgrade, and UDP discovery.

R2231.rule: Publish a guest's files under the origin the guest dialled, taken from its own Host header (readMirrorOrigin), never from peer.localAddress.

R2232.rule: Never trust a router's success response on its word; verify the port mapping before reporting it as opened.

R2233.rule: Before requesting a port mapping, call GetSpecificPortMappingEntry to check whether another client already owns that port.

R2234.rule: Skip any port owned by another client, or by this computer on a different internal port, and never request it from the router.

R2235.rule: After the router accepts a port, read the mapping back once and probe the public side through NAT loopback with a one-time token before treating the port as open.

R2236.rule: If the router-probe answer is anything other than this server's token, try another port; if there is no answer, report the status as unknown.

R2237.rule: Re-check both the mapping ownership and the probe every half hour during renewal, including for permanent leases.

R2238.rule: When removing a port mapping, delete only an entry that still belongs to this computer.

R2239.rule: When the router refuses a requested port, request a different port.

R2240.rule: Stop searching for a port only when the router stops answering (NO_ANSWER or timeout).

R2241.rule: When the router returns error 724 (SamePortValuesRequired), restrict port attempts to this computer's own port.

R2242.rule: List the public address even when no port was opened on the router.

R2243.rule: When no router answered, look up the public address via https://api.ipify.org, but only if the user has chosen that lookup and only while the router is wanted.

R2244.rule: In service tests, mock the public-address lookup and never let a test reach it.

R2245.rule: Open a host's screen with ElectronScreenController.createDetached(hostScreenId), outside the id-keyed cache.

R2246.rule: For any IPC a screen window sends that names its screen by id, first resolve the target from the sender's webContents rather than from the id.

R2248.rule: When calling destroyInstance, drop only the cache entry for that instance itself.

R2249.rule: Apply the waiting-request caps (8 total, 4 per sender) only to internet requests; never cap LAN requests or requests from a site behind one router.

R2250.rule: Do not apply the internet-only cap of eight waiting requests to LAN guests.

R2251.rule: Generate the QR code with qr-image svgObject in the main process on demand, encoding plain host:port and never a link.

R2252.rule: Decode QR codes with jsqr, imported lazily in the guest page.

R2253.rule: Read this memory before modifying screenMirrorService.ts's gate, translate(), the link/incoming maps, or the router lifecycle.

R2254.rule: When a screen comes up blank after restart, check the console for a SyntaxError from parseJsonSafely before blaming the sync-group logic.

R2255.rule: When the "Dropping invalid on-screen slide entry" error appears, investigate where the invalid entry originated rather than treating the guard as the bug.

R2256.rule: In any screen page, never write settings to disk; screen pages only take settings in from their context copy.

R2257.rule: A screen page must never originate a setting; only the presenter decides settings.

R2258.rule: A new screen-side handler must not call any function ending in `sendScreenMessage` with a setting it read itself.

R2259.rule: When a screen draws with a new setting, read it through `appLocalStorage` under a key the presentation rule matches, so the push carries it, rather than adding a dedicated message.

R2260.rule: A setting that is a whole layer's state must be listed in `LAYER_STATE_SETTING_NAMES` (or its prefix list), so it is not sent twice to every present.

R2261.rule: When gliding a selected row into view on a screen, count the glide's duration in screen heights, not in pixels, so each window (Mini Screen, projector) glides on its own layout.

R2262.rule: During a screen glide, call markProgrammaticScroll on every animation frame so the scroll-sync quiet window stays active and the glide is not sent out as the operator's scroll.

R2263.rule: Stop a screen glide immediately when the operator scrolls with the wheel or presses a key (when input occurs after the glide started).

R2264.rule: When a new selection is made, cancel any in-progress glide on the same scroller before starting the new one.

R2265.rule: When gliding a selected row into view, scroll only the screen's own view and do not scroll any ancestor scrollable containers.

R2266.rule: Do not implement Foreground Screen Show by capturing screen N's window (for example with getMediaSourceId, getDisplayMedia, or desktopCapturer); draw N's content from its state instead.

R2267.rule: Do not show a screen inside itself in Foreground Screen Show.

R2268.rule: Do not allow Foreground Screen Show to form a loop between screens.

R2269.rule: Allow only one level of Foreground Screen Show nesting; a copy must not nest further.

R2270.rule: Keep the screen-show frame helper light because ScreenManager imports it, and pass the setting and camera readers in rather than importing them.

R2271.rule: The screen-show frame page must send nothing to its parent except its init message.

R2272.rule: Set color-scheme to normal on both the screen-show iframe and the frame's root element so the copy stays transparent.

R2273.rule: Give the Screen Show panel isCommonStyle: false instead of the text overlays' common style.

R2274.rule: When fixing the sticky noSyncGroupMap echo guard on the live sync path, save and restore the guard around dispatch in ScreenManager.syncScreenManagerGroup.

R2275.rule: When changing the live sync path's echo guard, make sure no layer setter echoes a sync back asynchronously.

R2276.rule: When a lyric line wraps or overprints in some sessions but not others, diagnose it as a font registration race, not a CSS bug.

R2277.rule: Do not try to fix unregistered-font lyric measurement by waiting on `document.fonts.ready`.

R2278.rule: To determine which font a broken lyric card was measured in, read the `.ol-preview-line` inline `width` by hand in DevTools.

R2279.rule: When diagnosing a broken lyric card, check whether `style#lang-km` exists at the moment the slide is measured.

R2280.rule: Measure projector lyric layout on the real `screen.html` target.

R2281.rule: Do not measure projector lyric layout in the mini preview.

R2282.rule: Do not attempt to fix lyric line overflow with `height: auto !important` in `LyricAppDocumentStage0/1` stage CSS.

R2283.rule: When writing to secure storage, pass `true` as the `isImmediate` argument to `save`.

R2284.rule: Do not pass `isImmediate` as `true` for plaintext (`appHomeStorage`) writes.

R2285.rule: Scrub legacy cleartext secrets on every app launch.

R2286.rule: Never migrate legacy cleartext secrets into encrypted storage.

R2287.rule: When scrubbing legacy secrets, reset the fields that depend on a removed secret.

R2288.rule: When scrubbing legacy secrets, set `isAutoPlay` to false.

R2289.rule: When scrubbing legacy secrets, set `accessTokenExpiresAt` to 0.

R2290.rule: Perform secret scrubbing in the main process, not in renderer getters.

R2291.rule: Do not add a renderer-side cache for credentials.

R2292.rule: When a secure entry cannot be decrypted, delete that entry.

R2293.rule: When a credential may have been exposed, tell users to rotate it, not just re-enter it.

R2294.rule: When `setSecureSetting` receives a non-string value, return without writing; do not coerce it to null.

R2295.rule: When safe storage is unavailable, keep the secret value in main memory for the session only.

R2296.rule: When safe storage is unavailable, never write the secret value to disk.

R2297.rule: When safe storage is unavailable, delete any stale encrypted blob for that key.

R2298.rule: When safe storage is unavailable, render `SettingOthersSecureStorageWarningComp` in both Settings cards.

R2299.rule: When changing the scrub's field lists, change the main-process and renderer lists together.

R2300.rule: When a pick, ring, or SHOWS chip fails to find a control that is visibly on screen, suspect an ambiguous name first, before suspecting the depth budget or a re-render.

R2301.rule: When building a selector, if a named part has a same-named sibling, keep the name and append :nth-child(n) to it.

R2302.rule: When building a selector, if a named part has no same-named sibling, do not append an :nth-child index to it.

R2303.rule: Do not aim a press at a control whose exact name is shared by other shown controls.

R2304.rule: To test an edit to the selector code live, use the workaround described in dom-match-memoised-in-page, because the page memoises the runtime.

R2305.rule: Never rename an existing settingArchiveCatalog leaf id, because leaf ids are written into archive files.

R2306.rule: Read the settings archive manifest as raw bytes, never through fsReadFile.

R2307.rule: Never read credential values from the keychain or settings just to count them.

R2308.rule: Export credentials only into a password-protected settings archive.

R2309.rule: Import credentials only from a password-protected settings archive.

R2310.rule: Never include the data-folder choice, screen-mirror identity, guests, router mapping, mode, virtual-display access/TLS settings, ai-enabled, migration markers, one-off requests, chat sessions, the spend ledger, or live screen content in a settings archive.

R2311.rule: Turn on ai-enabled only knowingly, with the user's awareness that it opens the agent doors.

R2312.rule: Open the settings export and import dialogs only; do not tick, expand, or press Ok in them.

R2313.rule: Leave the final verification pass of the settings export and import dialogs to a person.

R2314.rule: When adding a new screen layer or setter that persists a whole-screens map, save it through persistOnScreenEntry.

R2315.rule: Do not persist a whole-screens map with a bare unlocking(...) + setSetting call in a manager setter, because those setters also run in the projector on every sync.

R2316.rule: Do not write the on-screen maps from screen.html or from saveScreenManagersSetting.

R2317.rule: When a map reads back empty while the file holds more than {}, rebuild it in the Presenter from its live managers (collectLive).

R2318.rule: When a map reads back empty while the file holds more than {}, skip the save in any window other than the Presenter.

R2319.rule: Never save an on-screen map as {} plus a single key.

R2320.rule: Before treating a reload as proven, check performance.timeOrigin or use Page.reload; do not rely on Ctrl+R over CDP.

R2321.rule: Do not dismiss a SyntaxError from parseJsonSafely in a screen or presenter console as noise; treat it as an unreadable on-screen map.

R2322.rule: Make the parse-failure path fail closed instead of returning {} to a caller that is about to persist it.

R2323.rule: When writing a style shared by slide previews, declare its own `box-sizing` explicitly rather than relying on the page's global CSS.

R2324.rule: When a slide preview and the editor disagree by a few pixels, first check which global CSS rule the shadow root is missing before changing the geometry.

R2325.rule: A website capture may only talk to the site it was asked for and the public internet; never to the local machine or anything else on the local network.

R2326.rule: Do not add a same-host or loopback exemption to the capture wall so the app can preview its own pages.

R2327.rule: Any change that widens `CAPTURE_REQUEST_URL_PATTERNS` must keep the `file:///*` wall pattern.

R2328.rule: Do not flip `webSecurity: false` to true as part of an unrelated change; flipping it is a separate change that needs a corpus of real website items.

R2329.rule: Do not merge the three capture/loading boxes (webCaptureHelpers, webPageHelpers, aiChatGuestHelpers) into one function with a "be careful" flag.

R2330.rule: When a tool must process content the model would otherwise paraphrase or retype, pass the tool the source (an address or file name) rather than the model's copy of the content.

R2331.rule: A draft tool's result must begin with the drafter's first line (e.g. "Drafted a song…"), never with a "Read …" prefix.

R2332.rule: When checking a drafted answer, read the buttons under the answer as well as the draft itself.

R2333.rule: Put new SongSelect frontend code in src/plugins/song-select/, not in feature directories.

R2334.rule: Do not hand-inject tokens or patch fetch to re-verify the SongSelect sign-in path in dev.

R2335.rule: To re-verify the SongSelect sign-in path in dev, click the "(dev) Use Mock Data" button beside Sign In.

R2336.rule: Keep the OAuth window-closed rejection message ("Sign in window was closed") and the renderer's message match for the "canceled" toast in sync.

R2337.rule: When importing markdown as a lyric, use Lyric.createWithContent rather than create-then-setContent.

R2338.rule: After testing the SongSelect import, delete the imported .owl test files.

R2339.rule: Before any long measurement, run `npm ls --depth=0 | grep -i "invalid\|missing"` to check for dependency drift between node_modules and the lockfile.

R2340.rule: Before running `coverage-gap.mjs` or `npm run lint` after a pull, check `npm ls --depth=0` for invalid entries.

R2341.rule: Before running `coverage-gap.mjs` or `npm run lint` after a pull, check for empty package folders in node_modules using `find`.

R2342.rule: In a pull routine, run `git stash pop` only if the preceding `git stash push` actually created a new stash.

R2343.rule: Before pushing a stash, record the stash count; pop only if the count increased after the push.

R2344.rule: Skip the stash entirely when `git status --short` shows an empty tree.

R2345.rule: After any stash pop, count conflict markers across the whole tree using `git grep -l '^<<<<<<< ' | wc -l`, never piping the output through `head`.

R2346.rule: A renderToStaticMarkup call must finish without anything inside it parsing HTML.

R2347.rule: In any component that renderToStaticMarkup reaches, never call a sanitizer or DOMParser in the component body or in a hook.

R2348.rule: In a component that renderToStaticMarkup reaches, run any sanitizer or DOMParser call before the render (for example, as a JSX prop written at the call site) or after it, never during it.

R2349.rule: A sanitizer call is allowed in a plain client component that renderToStaticMarkup does not reach.

R2350.rule: To observe the HTML parser's behaviour, call it from a setImmediate callback in an offscreen BrowserWindow with nodeIntegration enabled.

R2351.rule: When driving an app shortcut from an injected expression or a tool, dispatch the synthetic KeyboardEvent at `document` with `key`, `code`, and the modifier flags set.

R2352.rule: When dispatching a synthetic keyboard event for an app shortcut, set the `code` property in addition to `key`.

R2353.rule: When setting `code` for a single-character key on a synthetic keyboard event, use the physical-key form such as `KeyQ` or `Digit3`.

R2354.rule: Before assuming a shortcut can be driven by a synthetic event, check whether it is a renderer-registered shortcut or an Electron main-process menu accelerator.

R2355.rule: If a synthetic keyboard event for a shortcut does nothing, first check whether that shortcut is a main-process menu accelerator before debugging the event itself.

R2356.rule: When a shortcut's modifier is given in documentation text (e.g., "Ctrl"), send the modifier exactly as the text states rather than translating it per platform.

R2357.rule: When adding new translation keys, keep them statically readable: use a literal string per branch, not a key looked up from a table.

R2358.rule: Call tran() only inside a component body, an event handler, or a render function.

R2359.rule: Never call tran() in a module-level const.

R2360.rule: Never file a missing-key finding based on a static sweep alone.

R2361.rule: Before reporting a missing-key issue, confirm the actual console throw with the app running in an installed non-English language.

R2362.rule: Do not treat an added tran() call as verified until the page has been seen rendering in a non-English language.

R2363.rule: To verify translation changes, install a non-English language in the app, switch to it, and walk the changed screens.

R2364.rule: Before adding a translation key, check whether a case or whitespace variant of it already exists.

R2365.rule: To find dynamic tran(prop) sites, find components that call tran(<destructured prop>) and collect the literal values passed to their usages repo-wide.

R2366.rule: When grepping for translation keys ad hoc, merge pure literal + chains into one key, as the test does.

R2367.rule: When sweeping dictionary.json keys, match both quoted and unquoted key forms.

R2368.rule: Store only the transition effect at each level (slide, background, foreground), not any other data.

R2369.rule: When a transition is unticked, remove its entry from the store.

R2370.rule: Never write a default transition value into any store.

R2371.rule: Set `transitionEffect` on a datum only through `withTransitionEffect` or `toTransitionPart`.

R2372.rule: If reading a slide's transition sidecar fails, treat the transition as undefined and still show the slide; never block the slide.

R2373.rule: The screen window must never read the transition stores; transitions are resolved on the presenter and carried in the data.

R2374.rule: Animate each item out using the transition it came in with, not the incoming transition of another item.

R2375.rule: A `none` transition must be an instant cut in both directions.

R2376.rule: The `move` transition must use the `translate` CSS property.

R2377.rule: The `move` transition must never write the `left` property.

R2378.rule: The `move` transition must never push a sibling element.

R2379.rule: A zoom transition must clear its transform once at rest.

R2380.rule: When the marquee has no transition ticked, keep its edge slide instead of using the screen's Foreground effect.

R2381.rule: Keep the `.transition.json` sidecar in `FILE_EXTENSIONS` so it travels with rename and trash.

R2383.rule: Handle the `.transition.json` sidecar in `preDelete` so it is handled when a file is deleted.

R2384.rule: Include transition metadata in archives as the optional `transitionMetas` manifest field.

R2385.rule: Provide the transition row for colour swatches only in the Background Fills tab, via `ColorSwatchExtraMenuContext`.

R2386.rule: Gradient and pattern tiles must read the same `ColorSwatchExtraMenuContext` as colour swatches.

R2388.rule: A panel restored open on start-up must listen to `SCREEN_EFFECT_CHANGED_EVENT` to update its labels.

R2389.rule: A new way of showing a slide, background, or overlay needs no extra transition work if it goes through the existing choke points.

R2390.rule: Any new file-copying path must carry `.transition.json` the same way it carries `.bg.json`.

R2391.rule: When driving the app live, touch a file after rewriting it in place so Vite does not serve a stale module.

R2392.rule: Close only a browser tab that you yourself opened.

R2393.rule: To close a tab, click the uid that take_snapshot returned for that tab.

R2394.rule: Never close a tab by matching a label that another tab may share.

R2395.rule: Reuse one test tab for the whole run instead of opening and closing tabs.

R2396.rule: If the chatbot session store must be repaired, run a watchdog that rewrites the session while the window reloads.

R2397.rule: Do not change the `typescript` dependency alias (it points to the TS 6 API package), because typescript-eslint needs it.

R2398.rule: When upgrading to TypeScript 7, bump the version of the `@typescript/native` dependency, not the `typescript` dependency.

R2399.rule: Do not use `npx tsc` to determine which TypeScript compiler version is in use.

R2400.rule: To check the TypeScript compiler version, run `node node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc -v`.

R2401.rule: Once typescript-eslint supports TypeScript 7, change the `typescript` dependency back to a plain `"typescript": "^7.x"`.

R2402.rule: Before matching words in Khmer or other unspaced-script text, strip zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF) from the text.

R2403.rule: When matching or counting words of a script written without spaces, normalise the zero-width characters first.

R2404.rule: When matching or counting words of a script written without spaces, never treat a single whitespace-separated token as one word.

R2405.rule: When testing whether unspaced-script input is a bare name, bound the test by length, sentence marks and lead words (such as `nameAskLead`).

R2406.rule: When testing whether unspaced-script input is a bare name, do not bound the test by word count.

R2407.rule: Write regexes that match zero-width characters from a script file, not through the Edit tool, to avoid the literal character being written into the file.

R2408.rule: Do not delete a useAppCurrentRef guard as redundant just because the value it tracks is already in scope.

R2409.rule: After an await, before setting state, compare the closed-over prop to the useAppCurrentRef's .current, and bail or re-run on mismatch.

R2410.rule: Treat any useAppCurrentRef whose .current is compared to a closed-over value after an await as a race guard, not as clutter.

R2411.rule: On a mismatch after an await, drop the stale result when the re-feed itself re-runs the read.

R2412.rule: On a mismatch after an await, re-run the read when the result is still owed to the new subject.

R2413.rule: Declare the useAppCurrentRef above the useCallback that reads it.

R2414.rule: Write verse items always into Note.getDefault({ isBaseSession: true }), the Default note of the Default session, regardless of which session the Bible Notes list is showing.

R2415.rule: Make NoteItem.toJson() spread ...this.originalJson first, before any other fields, so fields it does not carry are not erased from unrelated items.

R2416.rule: Make NoteItem.update() preserve fields it does not carry, the same way toJson() does, by spreading originalJson.

R2417.rule: Paint verse marks with the CSS Custom Highlight API (CSS.highlights and ::highlight() rules), never with wrapper spans.

R2418.rule: Drive verse-mark repaints with one MutationObserver per bible view, not by enumerating invalidation triggers.

R2419.rule: Do not render verse items through BibleNoteItemRenderComp.

R2420.rule: Have readNoteFileScan gate the lazy bible-note import on text items alone.

R2421.rule: Never let a directory containing only verse items load lexical or excalidraw into a reader window.

R2422.rule: Make a verse row's drag serialize a bibleItem, not a note item.

R2423.rule: Build the verse row's drag bibleItem synchronously from the verse key.

R2424.rule: Do not offer a Duplicate action on verse rows.

R2425.rule: Never restate the highlight/comment colour palette in TypeScript; read it from the CSS custom properties.

R2426.rule: In SCSS, do not combine several & selectors in one selector (such as &--comment &__text); write the full selector out.

R2427.rule: When a mark row is clicked, open its verse as another bible view via openVerseBibleItem and addBibleItemRight.

R2428.rule: Do not use setLookupContentFromBibleItem when opening a mark row's verse.

R2429.rule: Put comment editing on the mark's ⋮ menu, not on a click of the mark.

R2430.rule: In the Bible Notes panel, read the controller with use(BibleItemsViewControllerContext), not the useBibleItemsViewControllerContext hook, which throws without a provider.

R2431.rule: Apply useBibleFontFamily(bibleKey) to the whole verse block, not only to the marked words.

R2432.rule: Apply useBibleFontFamily(bibleKey) to the comment editor and the hover tooltip as well.

R2433.rule: Do not rely on parsing the verse key out of the display title; carry verseKey in VerseCommentTargetType.

R2434.rule: Portalled surfaces (the selection toolbar and the comment hover tool) must set data-bs-theme themselves from useThemeSource().

R2435.rule: During a video loop crossfade, keep the outgoing video copy at full opacity underneath until the fade finishes.

R2436.rule: Do not fade both stacked video copies at once during a loop crossfade; only the incoming copy should fade.

R2437.rule: Build the second stacked video copy for a looping background once and reuse it on every lap, rather than creating a new element each lap.

R2438.rule: After a loop crossfade ends, pause the element that just ended, seek it back to 0, and park it at opacity 0 inside the same #background.

R2439.rule: When clearing a background, remove all children of #background, not only the last child.

R2440.rule: When removing a parked video copy, do not use animOut; remove it directly.

R2441.rule: Two video elements may share the same id generated by genVideoIDFromSrc; this is acceptable.

R2442.rule: Only the most recent render() call should put a background up.

R2443.rule: Drop a background render that has been overtaken by a newer render, and release its media player.

R2444.rule: When removing old elements, call releaseMediaElement on every video[id^="video-"] element being removed.

R2445.rule: To add a View menu entry, extend the `view` bucket.

R2446.rule: Never hard-code View menu entries in `electronMenu.ts`.

R2447.rule: Widget names (the View menu labels) must be unique per page.

R2448.rule: When resetting widget sizes, blank `style.flexGrow` on the panes before re-rendering.

R2449.rule: Never reuse a virtual display number once it has been assigned.

R2450.rule: When HTTPS is enabled for the mirror port, never stop serving plain HTTP, because screen windows, the MP4 compositor and TVs depend on it.

R2451.rule: Add every query key that `toScreenSrc` writes to `DEV_VIEWER_PAGE_QUERY_KEYS` in `virtualDisplayProtocol.ts`.

R2452.rule: Every `electron/` module that `src/` imports for a value must pass the dev viewer allowlist.

R2453.rule: Test a viewer change on the LAN address, never only on 127.0.0.1.

R2454.rule: When adding a new Date field to screen data, let it pass through `translate()` untouched and revive it from ISO text in `receiveSyncScreen`.

R2455.rule: In `translate()`, map page-relative app addresses like `/assets/...` with `toAppFile` before the absolute-path branch.

R2456.rule: Any new caller that shows a screen early must import `MiniScreenComp` first so the presenter can answer the bootstrap request.

R2457.rule: Stop any scratch instance holding port 39241 before running the screenMirrorService test gate.

R2458.rule: Give a scratch dev copy its own `screen-mirror-port` setting so it does not share a port with the user's app.

R2459.rule: Measure the viewer's module graph again with a resource log when the screen page starts importing from new places.

R2460.rule: Set `muted` as a property on a camera `<video>` element, not as an attribute, or the browser will refuse to start it.

R2461.rule: Test browser camera features with `electron . --use-fake-device-for-media-stream` to avoid the "Device in use" error.

R2462.rule: A delayed WebSocket close must never keep the old viewer authorized or clear its replacement's cameras.

R2463.rule: Place a screen with no display via `getPlacementDisplay`, which must never return a virtual display.

R2464.rule: Never forward `visible` or `init` packets from a viewer to the presenter.

R2465.rule: Before diagnosing a viewer sync bug, stop any running slide show or sample the viewer over time.

R2466.rule: Never let a viewer show a screen; viewers may only watch, and interaction may only hide a screen.

R2467.rule: Play virtual display sound only through the stream on the screen page, never locally on the presenter.

R2468.rule: Store the HTTPS certificate in the secure setting `virtual-display-tls` and generate it only the first time HTTPS is turned on.

R2469.rule: Emit 'listening' on the non-listening HTTP/HTTPS servers so Node starts its request timeout checks.

R2470.rule: Allow at most 8 waiting browsers across all virtual displays at once.

R2471.rule: When adding an import for a file that does not exist yet, create the file first and add the import afterward.

R2472.rule: If a module stays stuck with a failed import resolution after its file exists, touch vite.config.ts and reload the page.

R2473.rule: To check whether a module is still stale after a failed import resolution, curl its URL on the dev server and confirm it returns JavaScript rather than an HTML error page.

R2474.rule: When the served module is an old but valid version, touch the source file itself before touching vite.config.ts.

R2475.rule: To confirm which version of a module the dev server serves, fetch it from inside the page with a cache-busting query and grep for the expected symbol, rather than using curl.

R2476.rule: If appending a byte to an empty cached module does not clear it, touch vite.config.ts.

R2477.rule: When adding a call to a function, put its import in the same edit as the first use.

R2478.rule: When a file was edited in separate edits that left the dev server with an in-between version, touch every such file before a live check.

R2479.rule: After a git stash, pull, and apply that involved untracked files, immediately touch vite.config.ts.

R2480.rule: When a feature that exists on disk appears missing in the running app, fetch the served module and grep it before concluding anything.

R2481.rule: When a window fails with a 504 on a /node_modules/.vite/deps/ chunk, append a newline to vite.config.ts to make the Vite dev server restart and re-optimize deps.

R2482.rule: After touching vite.config.ts to restart the dev server, wait about 5 seconds before continuing.

R2483.rule: After the dev server restarts from the vite.config.ts touch, restore vite.config.ts to its original contents.

R2484.rule: Confirm that the Vite dep-optimizer restart worked by checking that browserHash in node_modules/.vite/deps/_metadata.json changed.

R2485.rule: Do NOT restart `npm run dev` to fix a dep-optimizer 504, because it kills the user's running Electron app.

R2486.rule: For a dependency that is imported lazily (dynamic import), add it to optimizeDeps.include in vite.config.ts so it is pre-bundled.

R2487.rule: Do NOT add open-lyric-plugin-km-kh to optimizeDeps.include, because its assets must resolve via /@fs/ rather than .vite/deps/.

R2488.rule: Include open-lyric/internal in optimizeDeps.include so it is pre-bundled once and shared by the app and language plugins.

R2489.rule: When a new language file imports a package, apply the same optimizeDeps include/exclude treatment to that package.

R2490.rule: Do NOT verify an optimized dep by requesting it with another file's ?v= hash, since each optimized file has its own hash.

R2491.rule: After a dependency upgrade, compare grep -c counts of a new symbol in node_modules/.vite/deps/<dep>.js against node_modules/<dep>/dist before debugging a feature.

R2492.rule: After a dependency upgrade, compare the vite process start time against the dependency's mtime to detect a stale pre-bundle before debugging a feature.

R2493.rule: If a dependency was upgraded while vite:dev was running, touch vite.config.ts and then reload the Electron windows.

R2494.rule: When a test file fails with a DOM-missing error because its imports reach appProvider, add the `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma to that test file.

R2495.rule: When adding a jsdom pragma exposes new failures in a test, fix the test's content (mocks and assertions), not only its environment.

R2496.rule: Treat a "(0 test)" line in vitest output as a failure, not as a skipped test.

R2497.rule: Any new or failing test whose imports reach `appProvider`, `FileSource`, or React components needs the `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma.

R2498.rule: To find latent DOM-dependency cases, run all pragma-less test files together in one vitest invocation.

R2499.rule: When `npm run lint` fails with every src test file erroring with "reading 'config'" or "Vitest failed to find the runner", re-run the command before investigating.

R2500.rule: When checking `npm run lint` results, read the log body rather than relying on the exit code.

R2501.rule: In DOM event tests, append the input element to `document.body`, dispatch the event, and remove the input in a `finally` block.

R2502.rule: In tests of file-path injection, assert the event's effect with `Object.hasOwn(file, 'appFilePath')` rather than reading the property alone.

R2503.rule: Check the refused-path case in DOM event tests with an attached input, so a negative assertion does not pass merely because the event reached nobody.

R2504.rule: When a test needs vi.resetModules(), pin the electron mock by requesting it before any reset, using a top-level `import 'electron';` alongside a static `import { electronMockState } from './testElectronModule';`.

R2505.rule: When pinning the electron mock before a vi.resetModules() reset, do not use a per-test `await import('./testElectronModule')` inside the test.

R2506.rule: When a test only needs different `isDev`/`isWindows` values per case, do not call vi.resetModules() at all.

R2507.rule: When a test needs different `isDev`/`isWindows` values per case, mock `./electronHelpers` with getters over a `vi.hoisted()` object.

R2508.rule: When a test uses a `vi.hoisted()` object with getters to vary `isDev`/`isWindows`, flip those fields in `beforeEach`.

R2509.rule: When the electron mock instance is pinned and a test needs a return value, use `mockReturnValueOnce` instead of `mockReturnValue`.

R2510.rule: When the electron mock instance is pinned and a test sets a default return value with `mockReturnValue`, re-set that default in `beforeEach`.

R2511.rule: Take the capture size of a website item from the `WEBSITE_CAPTURE_SIZE_ATTR` attribute in the markup, not from layout measurements.

R2512.rule: Make the website frame the only hit target inside a website canvas item's box.

R2513.rule: Set `pointer-events: none` on every descendant element of a website canvas item's box.

R2514.rule: Do not add a child element inside a website canvas item's box unless it has `pointer-events: none`.

R2515.rule: Do not remove the `pointer-events: none` from the `#background` container in `ScreenBackgroundManager.containerStyle`.

R2517.rule: In tests that wait for a website screenshot, wait with `setTimeout(…, 25)` rather than awaiting `Promise.resolve()` twice.

R2518.rule: Do not use `unlocking` to implement the screenshot capture concurrency cap.

R2519.rule: Cache a local file's screenshot by the md5 of its bytes and do not expire that entry.

R2520.rule: Never use a file's mtime as its identity for screenshot caching; use it only to memoise the md5.

R2521.rule: Import `fileHelpers` lazily in the capturing helpers module.

R2522.rule: Import `fileHelpers` only when the url is a `file:` url.

R2523.rule: Drop stale cached screenshots of a file by md5, not by cache key.

R2524.rule: When adding a new close path for a resizable widget, mutate the DOM (set the sibling's style.flexGrow) before calling setDisablingSetting.

R2525.rule: Never persist a resizable widget's disabled flag without also persisting the pane sizes around it.

R2526.rule: On a Windows-on-ARM64 dev machine, build the win-arm64 yt-dlp binary with a native ARM64 Python.

R2527.rule: On a Windows-on-ARM64 dev machine, build the win (x64) yt-dlp binary with an x86_64 Python run under emulation, installed via `uv python install cpython-3.13-windows-x86_64-none`.

R2528.rule: When building the win (x64) yt-dlp binary, set YTDLP_BUILD_DIR to a directory of its own, because the work dir's venv is reused as it is.

R2529.rule: Build the linux-arm64 yt-dlp binary in WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with YTDLP_BUILD_DIR on the Linux filesystem.

R2530.rule: Build the linux yt-dlp binary only on an x86_64 Linux host, because WSL has no x86_64 emulation.

R2531.rule: To determine the architecture of a Windows yt-dlp.exe on an ARM64 host, read its PE header instead of trusting the -v output (u32 at 0x3c, then u16 at +4: 0x8664 is AMD64, 0xaa64 is ARM64).

R2532.rule: Verify each new yt-dlp binary using the app's own flags (toYtDlpRuntimeArgs in src/server/appHelpers.ts) and the pack's ffmpeg and qjs.

R2533.rule: When `git add` on Windows records a new Linux yt-dlp binary as 100644, run `git update-index --chmod=+x` on it so it is committed as 100755.

R1.rule: Never hardcode ATT&CK tactic or technique tables; derive them from the pinned dataset instead.

R2.rule: Write the pinned dataset file attack/enterprise-attack.json only via tools/attack_data.py, never by any other means.

R3.rule: Never rewrite the store when the ATT&CK pin moves.

R4.rule: Do not treat prose-based technique extraction as a migration shim; keep it as a permanent code path.

R5.rule: When auditing, lift a single legacy entry only via an improvement record, never by rewriting the store.

R6.rule: When no source states the access vector, do not map a technique for it.

R7.rule: If the honest technique mapping would be empty, do not publish the entry.

R8.rule: For routine in-repo fixes, carry the full publishing chain end-to-end (sync main, stage, commit, second sync, push with retry, poll auto-merge, poll deploy-site, probe the live URL) without stopping to ask.

R9.rule: Never stop at a "ready to commit/push" state to ask the user for permission before committing or pushing a routine in-repo fix.

R10.rule: Whenever memory files were modified, include `.claude/memory/` in the staged files.

R11.rule: Pause and ask before performing destructive operations such as force-push or deleting branches or state files.

R12.rule: Pause and ask before making shared-infrastructure changes such as editing workflows, branch protection, or CNAME.

R13.rule: Pause and ask before making editorial-policy changes unless there is a clear request for them.

R14.rule: Do not remove the `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` setting or its memory-path allowlist.

R15.rule: If a memory write triggers a permission prompt, widen the allowlist glob in `.claude/settings.json` rather than accepting the prompt.

R16.rule: Prefer the `Write` and `Edit` tools when modifying memory files.

R17.rule: Commit memory changes to git; memory that is not committed to git is treated as not saved, since the container is destroyed after every run.

R18.rule: Record every change in behavior only in prompts/CHANGELOG.md, never in other files.

R19.rule: Do not write version-history annotations (e.g., "(v2.53)", "NEW in v2.66", "removed in v2.64") into prompts, agent definitions, CLAUDE.md, docs, config comments, or tool output strings.

R20.rule: Put version history in the CHANGELOG entry and state rules in the file itself without version framing.

R21.rule: When editing a rule, keep operational rationale such as dated incident references inline; only remove version framing.

R22.rule: Every entry must carry exactly one rating.

R23.rule: For non-triage entry kinds, include the NATO Admiralty `classification: {reliability, credibility}` block.

R24.rule: For triage entry kinds, carry `org_triage` instead of the Admiralty block only while `config/org-profile.yaml` configures a triage scheme.

R25.rule: When no triage scheme is configured, include the Admiralty block on vulnerability entries.

R26.rule: Never hand-edit the rule blocks rendered from config by `compose_prompts.py`.

R27.rule: Do not count a same-day press write-up of a single lab report as a second source.

R28.rule: When assessing independence, open the second source and check what it observed itself rather than counting sources.

R29.rule: If every fact in an entry traces back to the first source, mark the entry `single-source` with credibility 2.

R30.rule: Still cite a same-day press write-up that is not counted as a second source.

R31.rule: Count a second source as genuine only if it performs its own determination.

R32.rule: Treat a KEV listing as a genuine second source relative to a vendor advisory.

R33.rule: Put defensive role framing at the top of a sub-agent spawn message.

R34.rule: Do not hide what the work is when framing a sub-agent spawn; reframing the agent's role is acceptable.

R35.rule: When spawning a sub-agent, point it at the coverage file instead of listing covered breach or actor names inline.

R36.rule: Checkpoint the findings YAML every 3–4 items during a sub-agent spawn.

R37.rule: Record spawn terminations for each classifier fire.

R38.rule: When a spawn is terminated by the classifier, retry it once.

R39.rule: If the retry is also tripped, re-frame the spawn using defensive framing, no quoted exploit prose, and checkpointing.

R40.rule: If the re-framed spawn also fails, record it as a failed spawn.

R41.rule: Set verification.confirmation_waived only when the failed spawn was the confirmation pass.

R42.rule: Never count a failed spawn as CLEAN.

R43.rule: Never block the run because a spawn failed.

R44.rule: Report a classifier trip as a classifier trip, including the retry count.

R45.rule: Never report a classifier trip as "the mechanism failed".

R46.rule: On 5.5 models, when a decline occurs, record the refusal category along with the request id when the harness shows it.

R47.rule: Wait for the harness notification while a sub-agent is still writing instead of declaring it dead.

R48.rule: Treat a spawn as stalled only after 60 minutes with no write under work/<run-id>/ and no notification.

R49.rule: Before starting a recovery spawn, check that it can advance the gate it exists to protect.

R50.rule: When a paragraph rests on one source, cite that source only once in the paragraph.

R51.rule: Measure the main-analysis word count with the gate's own method (strip link markup with the MD_LINK_TEXT_RE substitution, then collapse whitespace).

R52.rule: When replacing a changelog entry near the word bound, draft the replacement in a scratch file and count its words before applying it.

R53.rule: When rewriting a changelog entry already at 548 words, cut as many words as the rewrite adds.

R54.rule: Cite the page that actually carries a given fact, not a related page.

R55.rule: When a deep read returns a claim table, cite the table's URL for that row rather than the entry's primary URL.

R56.rule: Give each deep-read spawn its own work/<run-id>/<tag>/ scratch directory.

R57.rule: When an update drops detail that the summary and actions[] still claim, restore that detail.

R58.rule: Never leave the summary asserting detail that the body no longer contains.

R59.rule: When two entries in the window carry the same action text, keep the action only on the entry that covers both cases.

R60.rule: Read affected, fixed, and patch-timing facts from structured fields in vulnerability records, never from the human-readable summary.

R61.rule: For CSAF records, determine affected and fixed status from the vulnerabilities[].product_status fields (known_affected, fixed, known_not_affected, under_investigation).

R62.rule: Never conclude that no fix exists for a CSAF vulnerability without checking its remediations[] array.

R63.rule: Identify the real patch in CSAF records as the remediations[] entry whose category is vendor_fix.

R64.rule: For Red Hat package_state[] rows, use the row's fix_state field as the verdict on whether the product is affected.

R65.rule: Transcribe the verdict field, not mere membership in an enumerated list, when recording a vulnerability's status.

R66.rule: When a discloser's 'CNA score' value looks like an outlier, spot-check it against the CNA's own containers.cna.metrics.

R67.rule: Store the CVSS BASE score in cves[].cvss.

R68.rule: Before calling two CVSS scores contradictory, check the linked vector for E:, RL:, or RC: metrics, since a displayed score may be temporal.

R69.rule: Read every element of the CNA's cna.metrics array, not just the first.

R70.rule: Never rank CVSS scores across different CVSS versions.

R71.rule: When multiple legitimate CVSS figures exist, put the chosen number in cves[].cvss.

R72.rule: When multiple legitimate CVSS figures exist, record the reconciliation (which body and which scale) in sourcing_note.

R73.rule: Do not treat an OSV 404 for an ecosystem-less product (such as a Joomla extension or firmware) as the CVE being unreachable.

R74.rule: Store cves[].epss as the FIRST.org EPSS probability, a decimal in [0, 1].

R75.rule: Never store an EPSS percentile or percentage in cves[].epss.

R76.rule: Divide an EUVD EPSS figure by 100 before storing it in the EPSS field.

R77.rule: Never put a provenance suffix such as '(EUVD)' into a numeric field.

R78.rule: Take the EPSS value from the API's epss field, never from its percentile field.

R79.rule: When correcting an EPSS entry, convert its units and preserve the entry's own as-of value.

R80.rule: Do not silently replace an EPSS entry's value with today's number when correcting it.

R81.rule: Keep the shipped config/branding.yaml and the loader DEFAULTS in sync so the built site stays byte-identical.

R82.rule: Treat the config list for feeds.sector_slices and trends.cohorts as the complete set, and treat an empty list as no entries.

R83.rule: Never put site-identity literals in site/build.py.

R84.rule: Never put lens phrases in prompt prose outside ORG-PROFILE blocks.

R85.rule: Where a lens phrase would otherwise appear in prompt prose outside ORG-PROFILE blocks, write "the profiled constituency (§ Organization profile)" instead.

R86.rule: Never write a concrete organization's name, estate, or affiliation into config, README, prompts, or memory.

R87.rule: Make a lens change by editing the config and running tools/compose_prompts.py --write.

R88.rule: Never make a lens change by editing code or prompts.

R89.rule: For byte-diff comparisons of build changes, build both sides with PYTHONHASHSEED=0.

R90.rule: Before composing an entry, check every candidate CVE against the store-wide CVE index (state-summary.json cves ids), not only the 14-day prior_coverage read.

R91.rule: When a candidate CVE hits the store-wide index, grep entries/ for that CVE, read the covered entry, and decide whether to record an update or drop the candidate.

R92.rule: When evaluating a covered CVE, read the covered entry's body text, not only its cves[].status field.

R93.rule: Limit branding changes to config/branding.yaml.

R94.rule: Keep fonts on the system stack and never load an external webfont.

R95.rule: Separate elements with borders, not shadows.

R96.rule: Use small border radii.

R97.rule: Never use emoji in the site.

R98.rule: Never include IOCs on the site.

R99.rule: Use a single crimson accent colour.

R100.rule: Render every machine fact in the monospace font.

R101.rule: Design the interface dark-first.

R102.rule: Never re-enable "dlig" in heading font-feature-settings.

R103.rule: Keep "kern","liga" in heading font-feature-settings.

R104.rule: Add a :not(.b) guard to inline-token prose rules that share a class with a badge.

R105.rule: Never include the running (partial) ISO week in trends comparisons.

R106.rule: Compute trend deltas as the latest complete week compared with the prior week.

R107.rule: Render verification flags in a neutral colour.

R108.rule: Use red only for priority or exploited indicators.

R109.rule: Never hardcode classification doctrine; take classification badges and scheme text from config via _load_classification_scheme().

R110.rule: After any site/build.py renderer edit, re-check the document contract invariants.

R111.rule: Emit exactly one <h1> per page, except redirect stubs and meta-refresh pages.

R112.rule: Never skip heading levels on a page.

R113.rule: Never let embedded markdown keep its own heading level; pin it with render_markdown(..., heading_base=N).

R114.rule: Pass head_level when rendering run notes.

R115.rule: Pin entry bodies to h3.

R116.rule: Render day-brief section headers as <h2 class="sect">, not divs.

R117.rule: Keep ids unique within each page and make every #anchor resolve.

R118.rule: Give heading anchors the run id as anchor_prefix.

R119.rule: Emit #update-<at> anchors only on the entry permalink.

R120.rule: Pass anchor=False everywhere except the entry permalink.

R121.rule: Build finding anchors from the entry id, not the slug.

R122.rule: Give the bare #T… anchor only to the first occurrence of an ATT&CK technique.

R123.rule: Namespace repeated tactic anchors.

R124.rule: Make a matrix cell a link only when its directory row exists.

R125.rule: Measure contrast ratios against AA in both themes, with alpha compositing applied.

R126.rule: Composite translucent tints before computing a contrast ratio.

R127.rule: Make --text-muted clear 4.5:1 on --bg, --bg-elev, --bg-elev-2 and --kbd-bg.

R128.rule: Never de-emphasise text with opacity.

R129.rule: Use --text-muted to de-emphasise text instead of opacity.

R130.rule: Put all entry metadata in the labelled rail.

R131.rule: Place the run-dashboard link in the Record section of the rail, never under the title.

R132.rule: Make every rail table row a .frow with __l label and __v value parts.

R133.rule: Never give the entry rail its own scrollbar.

R134.rule: Never make the entry rail sticky.

R135.rule: Limit the stamps under the entry title to published and updated.

R136.rule: Make the updated stamp deep-link to the newest #update-<at> anchor.

R137.rule: Suppress the entry headline when it merely restates the title.

R138.rule: Never repeat the stored summary on the entry permalink header.

R139.rule: Give .ehead margin-bottom: 34px rather than placing the margin on .immediate-action.

R140.rule: Zero the first child of both entry columns so their tops align.

R141.rule: Define --entry-col, --entry-rail and --entry-gap on body.entry-detail inside the >=1100px media query.

R142.rule: Make .elede and .emeta use --entry-col, falling back to 100%.

R143.rule: Order entry body sections actionable-first.

R1.rule: Make each class and method either an Integration or an Operation, never both.

R2.rule: Do not make an Operation call other project or solution methods.

R3.rule: Operations may use framework methods and third-party libraries.

R4.rule: Do not put considerable logic inside an Integration method.

R5.rule: If a method contains considerable logic, do not make it call other project methods.

R6.rule: Integrations may contain trivial conditionals such as simple routing or guard-style early returns.

R7.rule: Do not mix logic and composition in the same method; split them into separate methods.

R8.rule: Cover Operations with focused unit tests.

R9.rule: Cover Integrations with a small number of integration or wiring tests.

R10.rule: Write the simplest code that solves the current, actual problem.

R11.rule: Do not add abstractions, generics, or extension points for hypothetical future requirements.

R12.rule: Do not design for reusability when something is used in only one place.

R13.rule: Do not make things configurable when a constant works for now.

R14.rule: Do not add parameters, interfaces, or indirection that serve no present purpose.

R15.rule: Make domain logic functionally pure: same inputs produce same outputs with no side effects.

R16.rule: Do not make domain logic depend on I/O, file access, network calls, UI interaction, or uninjected randomness or time.

R17.rule: Isolate I/O concerns at the edges of the system.

R18.rule: When domain logic needs an external value such as the current time, inject it as a parameter instead of reading it inside the logic.

R19.rule: Do not mix domain logic and I/O concerns.

R20.rule: Do not pass function call results or newly constructed objects directly as method arguments.

R21.rule: Assign a function call result or newly constructed object to a named variable before passing it as an argument.

R22.rule: The no-inline-construction rule does not apply to test code.

R23.rule: Use comments sparingly, if at all.

R24.rule: Put the reasoning behind a decision in the git commit message, not in code comments.

R25.rule: When a comment feels needed, first rename the method, class, or variable so the name carries that meaning.

R26.rule: Write a comment only if no name can express the meaning.

R27.rule: Do not write doc-block summaries that restate a well-named function's behavior.

R28.rule: Do not write module-header prose explaining the domain.

R29.rule: Never reference issue-tracker items or ADR/decision documents in code comments.

R30.rule: Never reference issue-tracker items or ADR/decision documents in commit messages.

R31.rule: Before writing any comment, try to express it through renaming instead.

R32.rule: If a constraint cannot live in a name, state it directly in its own words, never by pointing at an issue or ADR.

R33.rule: Review the diff for accumulated doc blocks before reporting.

R34.rule: Only validate and handle errors at system boundaries such as user input, external APIs, file I/O, and network calls.

R35.rule: Do not add defensive checks inside internal code already guaranteed correct by domain logic or the type system.

R36.rule: If a null or invalid state is unreachable given domain invariants, do not add a null check or guard just because the type system allows it.

R37.rule: Do not add try/catch blocks, fallbacks, or error branches for conditions that cannot occur in the current call context.

R38.rule: Trust framework and library guarantees.

R39.rule: Do not re-validate what the framework already ensures.

R40.rule: Prefer letting unexpected failures propagate and crash loudly (fail-fast) rather than silently swallowing them with defensive code.

R41.rule: Write the commit message subject as one very short sentence describing what was done.

R42.rule: Separate the commit message subject from the body with a blank line.

R43.rule: Write the commit message body as a short explanation of why the change was made.

R44.rule: You may skip the commit message body for small changes.

R45.rule: State the why of a commit in the message's own words.

R46.rule: Leave issue closing and ADR linkage to the tracker files and docs themselves, not to commit messages.

R47.rule: Do not use a leading underscore prefix on private field names in C# code (including Blazor @code blocks).

R48.rule: When writing or editing C# (including Blazor @code blocks), declare private fields without a leading underscore.

R49.rule: In multi-line boolean expressions, place the boolean operator at the start of the continuation line.

R50.rule: In multi-line boolean expressions, do not place the boolean operator at the end of the previous line.

R51.rule: When a boolean expression spans multiple lines, break the line before the operator.

R52.rule: Do not add Prettier or any Prettier-derived formatter to projects.

R53.rule: When scaffolding or configuring tooling, skip Prettier, its editor-extension recommendations, and eslint-config-prettier.

R54.rule: When scaffolding or configuring tooling, lint with ESLint alone.

R55.rule: If a scaffold tool bundles Prettier by default, remove Prettier from the generated setup.

R56.rule: Use oxlint instead of typescript-eslint wherever typescript-eslint cannot parse the project's TypeScript.

R57.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system (forms, web interfaces, government portals, setup wizards), show only the one next step and then wait for the user's feedback before continuing.

R58.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system, show the overall plan once at the beginning.

R59.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system, give exactly one step per response, plus the values needed for that step.

R60.rule: When guiding the user through a multi-step process in an external system, end each response by specifically stating which feedback is needed from the user.

R61.rule: Do not apply the one-step-at-a-time approach to analyses, evaluations, or documents; deliver those completely.

R62.rule: Store code and engineering standards in memory files rather than in CLAUDE.md.

R63.rule: When a new rule governs how to communicate or behave in every session, save it to CLAUDE.md.

R64.rule: Save a new code or engineering standard as a feedback memory.

R65.rule: When a new code or engineering ruleset is major, add a pointer line under the "Code & Engineering Standards" section of CLAUDE.md.

R66.rule: If unsure whether a new rule belongs in CLAUDE.md or in a feedback memory, ask the user.

R67.rule: Save user preferences and coding style to global memory at ~/.claude/memory/.

R68.rule: Before saving a memory, ask whether it would apply in any project or only in this one.

R69.rule: Save general memories (user preferences, coding style, working style) to global scope.

R70.rule: Save memories tied to a specific codebase (goals, decisions, constraints, external references) to project scope.

R71.rule: When asked to analyze or review something or find improvements, present the findings as a plan or list and stop there, without making changes.

R72.rule: Do not make code changes when asked to analyze or review, unless explicitly asked to implement them.

R73.rule: Treat requests like "find improvements", "review", "audit", or "what should be changed" as requests for analysis output, not implementation.

R74.rule: Only write code when the user explicitly says to apply, fix, implement, or do it.

R75.rule: After implementing a change, stop and report what changed.

R76.rule: Do not run tests, lint, typecheck, or builds after implementing a change.

R77.rule: Do not run end-to-end verification, such as the /verify skill or launching the app and driving it.

R78.rule: Do not execute test files you wrote as part of an implementation.

R79.rule: Do not run git commit until the user has reviewed the change and explicitly approved it, even if prior slices in the repo were committed one per issue.

R80.rule: Implement the code and any test files the task calls for, then report what changed and hand off to the user.

R81.rule: State in the report that the change is unverified rather than claiming passing checks.

R82.rule: Run verification or checks only when the user explicitly asks for them in that conversation.

R83.rule: When the user invokes /tdd, run only single targeted tests in the red-green loop, and never run full suites, builds, lint, or typecheck.

R84.rule: Ask for or wait for user approval before running git commit.

R85.rule: Close the completed ticket only after the git commit succeeds.

R86.rule: Do not let harness or skill prompts suggesting verification override the rule against running verification without user request.

R87.rule: Do not treat repo commit history patterns as authorization to run git commit.

R1.rule: Never run destructive Azure operations (such as az group delete or az resource delete) autonomously; instead, provide the command and ask the user to execute it manually.

R2.rule: Run non-destructive Azure operations (such as az keyvault secret set, az deployment group create, az keyvault secret show, or other read/write operations that are not destructive) directly without asking the user.

R3.rule: Before surfacing any backlog item as open or actionable during backlog review, verify its live GitHub issue state.

R4.rule: During any backlog review, batch-check the GitHub state of every issue number mentioned before presenting recommendations.

R5.rule: Only flag a backlog item as actionable if its GitHub issue is OPEN and either has no milestone or has a milestone matching the current sprint.

R6.rule: Never rely on backlog log files alone as the source of truth for issue status.

R7.rule: Treat GitHub Issues as the single source of truth for issue status.

R8.rule: For normal development, run the frontend only inside Docker via `docker compose up`.

R9.rule: For regular development work, never run `npm run dev` or any local Vite dev server.

R10.rule: For e2e mock-auth tests, start the stack with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=E2ETesting docker compose up sqlserver api -d`.

R12.rule: For e2e mock-auth tests, ensure a local `frontend/.env.e2e` file exists containing `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE=true`.

R14.rule: If a task creates or modifies a main functionality, the plan must include an e2e test for its happy path.

R15.rule: Write and run the e2e test before opening the PR; do not merely plan it.

R16.rule: When writing the task plan, list the happy path(s) for the feature.

R17.rule: When writing the task plan, define what the e2e test will assert for each happy path.

R18.rule: Include the e2e test as an explicit step in the task plan, not as an afterthought.

R21.rule: Every review finding with severity minor or higher, and every deferred intent, must be filed as a GitHub issue.

R22.rule: Do not treat backlogs or plan files as storage for findings or deferred items; they are supplementary only, and anything not in GitHub must be filed there.

R23.rule: When analysis produces findings or proposed deferrals, name a target milestone for them.

R24.rule: Once the user accepts a finding or deferral, create the GitHub issue(s) immediately, without waiting or deferring to a later session.

R25.rule: When reporting a deferral, reference the new GitHub issue number.

R26.rule: Never list deferred items only in plan files, backlogs, or conversation summaries.

R27.rule: Clear backlog files (code-review-backlog.md, ui-review-backlog.md, observed-issues.md, ui-review-skipped.md) after triaging them.

R28.rule: Batch the entries in backlog files (code-review-backlog.md, ui-review-backlog.md, observed-issues.md, ui-review-skipped.md) into themed GitHub issues at sprint close.

R378.rule: Acknowledge SpiceMainChannel and then open SpiceUsbRedirChannel.

R379.rule: Implement standard usbredir frame handling for HELLO, DEVICE_CONNECT, and INTERRUPT frames.

R394.rule: Before answering any reverse-engineering question, run the Captures KB query tool for the relevant topic.

R6.rule: Keep each memory entry terse, no longer than one screen.

R7.rule: When editing a shared memory file, also update your personal copy of it, and when editing a personal copy, also update the shared copy.

R16.rule: When diagnosing a site 500 error, check `docker logs --tail 30 ai-mms-web-1` for the message "Invalid command 'Header'".

R17.rule: Only look at `var/report/` for Magento-level fatals after ruling out the missing mod_headers cause.

R23.rule: Never propose dump-and-restore, direct replication, or other whole-database sync methods to reconcile local and remote databases in this project.

R24.rule: When the user reports local/remote DB drift or asks to "sync" databases, skip straight to drafting the migration SQL.

R25.rule: Before drafting a DB sync migration, ask the user what the target state should be (which fields/rows differ and which side is canonical).

R26.rule: Write the DB migration script as idempotent and limited to applying only the agreed changes.

R27.rule: Place production-bound DB migration scripts under `migrations/`.

R28.rule: Place local-only DB fixup scripts under `scripts/local-dev/`.

R1.rule: Read the project memory from the memory directory in the repository (not from ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/) when working on this project.

R2.rule: Write new memory entries to the memory directory in the repository, not to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/.

R3.rule: Load MEMORY.md, the index, before anything else when working with project memory.

R4.rule: After loading MEMORY.md, read only the memory entries relevant to the current task.

R5.rule: When writing a memory entry, record one fact per file and include the frontmatter block (name, description, metadata type).

R6.rule: For feedback and project memory entries, include a **Why:** line and a **How to apply:** line.

R7.rule: Link related memory entries to each other using the [[their-name]] syntax.

R8.rule: When creating a new memory entry, add a one-line pointer to it in MEMORY.md.

R9.rule: Before creating a new memory file, check whether an existing file already covers the same ground.

R10.rule: If an existing memory file already covers the same ground as a new fact, update that file instead of creating a new one.

R11.rule: Do not record in memory anything the repository already states, such as code structure, past fixes, or git history.

R12.rule: When a memory entry is found to be wrong, delete it rather than leaving it in place.

R13.rule: Never announce a count or a list in prose and then deliver the content as prose; if the text announces a count or list, render it as an actual list.

R14.rule: When announcing a count, render the items as a `<ul className="list-disc pl-6 space-y-1 text-foreground">` list.

R15.rule:
Render each list item as its own `
    • ` element, one per item.

R16.rule: Give each list item its own i18n key.

R17.rule: When singling out one item of several, name that item in the same sentence as the singling out.

R18.rule: Do not defer naming a singled-out item to a later paragraph; name it in the same sentence.

R19.rule: If you don't want to present a list, delete the announcement of the count or list instead of keeping it.

R20.rule: When fixing a flagged problem, find and fix every instance of the same class of problem, not only the one instance that was flagged.

R21.rule: After finishing a fix pass, re-run beginner-review as a subagent.

R22.rule: Scope the beginner-review re-run to only the rewritten keys, in both locales.

R23.rule: Do not declare a fix pass done or commit it before the beginner-review re-run has been completed.

R24.rule: Do not bolt an explanation into an existing sentence using dashes or parentheses; write it as a separate sentence.

R25.rule: Express each idea in its own sentence.

R26.rule: Do not treat the review finding count as a sign that the text has converged.

R27.rule: Stop reviewing only when a review round returns no defects, not when the finding count looks small.

R28.rule: Before shipping, find every sentence that quantifies over the whole course (e.g., "every lab", "each chapter", "from here on always").

R29.rule: Check each course-wide quantifying sentence against src/data/chapters.ts and the actual chapter files.

R30.rule: Write each course division as lowercase «частина» followed by a Roman numeral in Ukrainian (e.g., «частина III»), not with a capitalised «Частина» or an Arabic numeral.

R31.rule: Write course part 0 with the Arabic numeral `0`, since it has no Roman numeral form.

R32.rule: In English, capitalise «Part» when naming a course division (e.g., "Part I", "Parts 0 and I").

R33.rule: Use Roman numerals for course divisions in both Ukrainian and English, except for part 0.

R34.rule: Do not conclude that «Частина» should be capitalised when a numeral follows it; the numeral does not change the case.

R35.rule: Run the course-part lint and numbering checks to verify translations instead of relying on visual inspection.

R36.rule: When a course-part numbering or capitalisation issue is flagged in one place, search the whole course for the same issue and fix every instance.

R37.rule: When searching or matching these i18n strings, ignore differences between non-breaking spaces and regular spaces.

R38.rule: When using a `<Circuit>` component, always pass a `maxWidth` prop equal to the diagram's width.

R39.rule: When placing a description label above a `Meter` symbol, offset it at least ~32 units from the symbol's center.

R40.rule: When placing a label above a `Diode` symbol, leave at least ~26 units of clearance.

R42.rule: For every SVG, use `getBoundingClientRect()` to flag text overlapping other text, circles, symbols, or component rects, and text spilling outside the SVG rect.

R43.rule: For each SVG, report its scale (clientWidth/viewBox.width) and the computed font size of its text.

R44.rule: Aim for zero text overlaps and all diagram fonts between 13 and 16px, unless a larger font is an intentional display readout.

R45.rule: New chapters must ship with zero overlaps, since they have no baseline entry.

R46.rule: After an intentional, browser-verified diagram change, regenerate the visual baseline by running `UPDATE_BASELINE=1 npm run test:visual`.

R47.rule: If CI or Linux font metrics cause a grandfathered overlap to drift, regenerate the baseline on that platform.

R48.rule: Still run the overlap detector by hand while authoring diagrams, for fast feedback.

R49.rule: After building or editing any diagram, reload the user's dev page.

R50.rule: Run the getBoundingClientRect detector across all SVGs before saying the task is done.

R51.rule: Run `npm run test:visual` before shipping a diagram change.

R52.rule: Trust the getBoundingClientRect detector output over a screenshot glance and over passing jsdom gates.

R53.rule: The hand-check must include non-text graphical elements (path, circle, rect, line, polygon) against the SVG frame, not just text.

R54.rule: For each path, circle, rect, line, or polygon, convert its getBoundingClientRect to viewBox coordinates and flag any edge past 0..VB, allowing about 2px tolerance.

R55.rule: Run the non-text frame-edge check especially on hero illustrations, since they have no text.

R56.rule: Visually inspect each of a hero's four frame edges specifically, not just the overall composition.

R57.rule: Do not treat a check that the composition reads well as a check that nothing touches or crosses the frame edge.

R58.rule: Perform a visual and hand-check on every hero diagram as the primary verification, treating the automated gate only as a backstop.

R59.rule: Never position an element on a curved surface using a fixed literal y coordinate; compute its y from the surface curve instead.

R61.rule: For any scene diagram with a ground or sea, antennas, and rays, reuse the scene-earth.tsx component instead of building the scene from scratch.
